[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
The National Archives catalogue indexes Michael Glasgow, aged 40, a supernumerary seaman, on the sick list from 16 March 1797 with venereal gonorrhoea, subsequently discharged to his ship. No discharge date or name of that ship is supplied for Michael. The parent description identifies the journal as that of HMS Gladiator, kept by surgeon H Maybee from 5 January 1797 to 25 February 1798 while Gladiator served as a convalescent ship in Portsmouth Harbour. This identifies the treatment setting, not Michael’s normal ship.<ref>The National Archives, Discovery catalogue, [https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/details/r/C10568938 Michael Glasgow, aged 40, in HMS Gladiator medical journal, folios 3–4], ADM 101/103/1/1, folios 3–4 (reviewed 12 November 2026); catalogue description, original uninspected.</ref>

His birth is estimated about 1756–1757 solely from the catalogue age of forty; neither date nor birthplace is independently known.<ref>The National Archives, Discovery catalogue, [https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/details/r/C10568938 Michael Glasgow, aged 40, in HMS Gladiator medical journal, folios 3–4], ADM 101/103/1/1, folios 3–4 (reviewed 12 November 2026); catalogue description, original uninspected.</ref>

The journal context is described separately in the parent catalogue entry.<ref>The National Archives, Discovery, [https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/details/r/C4107154 ADM 101/103/1], journal of HMS Gladiator, H Maybee, 1797–1798; catalogue description, original uninspected.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
The recorded age 40 implies birth approximately 1756–1757, if accurate. [[Glasgow-1416|Michael Glasgow (Glasgow-1416)]], born 19 November 1741, would be 55 on 16 March 1797, a concrete age conflict; do not assign this record to him without evidence correcting the reported age. [[Glasgow-1410|Michael Glasgow (Glasgow-1410)]] was baptised in 1712 and [[Glasgow-1406|Michael Glasgow (Glasgow-1406)]] was already recorded in 1679, also incompatible with an accurate age 40. [[Glasgow-3911|Michael Glasgow (Glasgow-3911)]] belongs to the sixteenth century; [[Glasgow-3595|Michael Glasgow (Glasgow-3595)]] was born in 1815 and [[Glasgow-4252|Michael Glasgow (Glasgow-4252)]] in 1889. No compatible maintained Michael profile was established. Wider live duplicate search and the original journal remain outstanding, so this is a source-verification hold, not an authorized live creation.

Reviewed 12 November 2026 from The National Archives official Discovery catalogue/API description. The original manuscript was not inspected; the catalogue reports the item as not digitised and open. Open archival access does not mean online images exist. No live WikiTree or FamilySearch edit, merge or family attachment follows.

The Michael Glasgow in the separate 1756 Antigua discharge order is not identified with this man. The two descriptions do not establish a shared identity or kinship. The 1797 reported age would place that man’s birth around the time of the earlier order.
